text.p: Shares in British banking group Alliance & Leicster Plc retreated on their second day of trading on Tuesday amid cautious press comment following Monday's storming market debut.
The stock, which hit a peak of 578p on Monday, well above market expectations, was down 18p at 548-1/2 by 0706 GMT in volume of 52.9 million shares.

The Financial Times Lex column said the "odds favour an early correction" in A&L's share price, and that this was made even more likely by the "high number of carpet-baggers" that the flotation had attracted.
Noting that the stock had closed on a premium to Abbey National Plc in terms of its prospecting price-earnings ratio, it said a discount was more appropriate.

And it said it was "far from clear" that a bid would emerge soon, making it possible that the company would start spending its large cash pile -- in which case sentiment "could quickly seep away from the stock."
Abbey National shares, which set a record 823p on Monday on the back of the surge in Alliance & Leicester stock, were down 5p at 807-1/2 by 0738 GMT.
